The Case against Lee Dah Yeu (李大有) charged with
propagating Communism.

Lee Dah Yeu (李大有) alias Lau Chang (老忄) who was
arrested on the authority of a search warrant at No.1034 Dah
Yeu Li (大有里), Robison Road, during the course of a series
of raids conducted by the Municipal Police on communist bases
on the night of October 11/12 (Vide Daily Intelligence Report
of 12-10-32), is reported to be an active member of the Chinese
Communist Party in the Western District of Shanghai and his
duties comprised the directing of workers in demonstrations.
At the time of his arrest he was found to be in possession of
four copies of a handbill urging workers to join the Communist
Party. Prior to his arrest he was observed, during the course
of a watch kept on him by agents of this office, to accost
workers outside factories in the Western District. He is
generally known among workers by the name of Lau Chang (老忄)
which is borne out by the finding in his room of an invitation
card addressed to Chang Soong San (忄松山); while "Lee Dah Yeu"
is evidently an assumed name (Vide D.S. Moore's report of 15-10-32
as the alleyway in which he lived is called Dah Yeu Li (大有里),
the characters Dah and Yeu being identical.

However, he was not implicated by other individuals
arrested during recent communist raids and further investigations
made by the Municipal Police have failed to discover any fresh
evidence against him.

On 25-10-32, Lee Dah Yeu (李大有) together with
three other accused arrested at certain other places on the
same date, were temporarily handed over to the Chinese
Authorities at the request of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau
for interrogation. They were all returned some two weeks later,
the Chinese Authorities stating that they had nothing to charge

关于指控李大有（Lee Dah Yeu）传播共产主义的案件。

李大有（Lee Dah Yeu），别名老忄（Lau Chang），于10月11/12日晚工部局警察对共产主义据点实施的一系列突袭行动中，持搜查令在罗宾森路（Robison Road）大有里（Dah Yeu Li）1034号将其逮捕（参见1932年10月12日的每日情报报告），据报他是上海西区中国共产党的活跃成员，其职责包括指挥工人参加示威游行。被捕时，发现他持有四份呼吁工人加入共产党的传单。在被捕前，本处特工在对他进行监视的过程中，观察到他在西区工厂外与工人搭讪。他在工人中通常被称为老忄（Lau Chang），这一点在他房间内发现的一张写给忄松山（Chang Soong San）的邀请卡得到了证实；而“李大有”显然是一个化名（参见 D.S. Moore 1932年10月15日的报告，因为他居住的弄堂叫大有里，“大”和“有”这两个字完全相同）。

然而，在最近几次共产主义突袭行动中被捕的其他人并未牵连到他，且工部局警方的进一步调查也未能发现针对他的新证据。

1932年10月25日，李大有（Lee Dah Yeu）连同同日在其他地方被捕的另外三名被告，应上海公安局的要求，暂时移交给中国当局进行审讯。约两周后他们全部被送回，中国当局称没有理由指控

Upon appearing before court on 30-11-32 for judgment,
Lee Dah Yeu was found "not guilty". The decision was appealed
against and he was ordered to put up reliable security during
the period of appeal. He is still being detained in Pootoo
Road Station.

Although the police possess ample information
regarding Lee Dah Yeu's communist activities, further evidence
against him other than the communist literature found in his
possession, is not available. Therefore, it is suggested
that, unless the A/M.A. thinks otherwise, the appeal be withdrawn.

Raids on Communist Bases - Result of Court Proceedings

/ Four important members of the local Communist Party
who were arrested during a series of raids on October 11/12
in connection with communist activities in the Shanghai
Western District (Vide I.R. 12/10/32), appeared on remand
before the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court on October 25,
when they were ordered to be handed over to the Chinese
Authorities for a period of two weeks for investigation
on a charge of communist offences in Chinese controlled
territory.

诉讼程序。T.S.Lee 先生代表警方出庭。
Tseu Kyi Vang 先生代表上海公安局（S.P.S.Bureau）出庭。
Van Gee Sung 先生代表被告出庭。
Lee 先生：- 警方已对被告提出指控。查获的物品也在该被告位于租界的住所内发现。警方尚未查明被告是否曾参与任何共产主义活动，但在他身上发现了传单。如果上海公安局希望将被告移交给他们，他们必须首先证明他涉及发生在中国领土内的罪行。
Tseu 先生：- 与此案有关的一些被告已由中国当局羁押。他们与其他四名被告有关联，我们要求将所有这些人移交给公安局两周以进行调查。如果在那段时间结束时，我们发现他们涉及中国当局管辖范围内的任何罪行，他们将据此被起诉。如果他们涉及租界内的任何罪行，那么他们将在此法庭就这些罪行被起诉和审判。
主审法官：- 既然这里已经对他们提出了指控，为什么还要将他们移交两周？
Tseu 先生：- 我们希望让他们与目前在押的其他人对质。我请求将被告移交两周。

Proceedings:- Mr. Lea appeared for the Police.
Miss Ts Ling appointed for the accused.
Mr. Lea:- The accused is charged under Articles
2 and 6 of the laws governing the punishment of persons who com-
mit acts with intent to injure the Republic of China. At 11.15.pm
on the 11th October, 1932, Headquarters of the Police received
information that a Communist named Lau Tsang was living at No.
1034, Dah Yuen Li, Macao Road. A warrant was applied for and
the detectives went to the house. The room was locked when
the Police arrived and the door was forced open and the accused
arrested, and some pamphlets found on the bed. The Police also
found an invitation card bearing the name of "Tsang Soo San".
When questioned the accused denied that his alias was Lau Tsang.
The accused has been to the P.S.Bureau, and I ask the Court to
remand the case pending further enquiries at the P.S.Bureau.
Miss Ts Ling:- There is no need for enquiries
at the P.S.Bureau. If they had evidence against him, they
would have kept him there, instead of handing him back to this
Court.
Accused Lee Dah Yeu:- When I left home I
lived at my friend's house at Nanking for three months and he
recommended me for a job in Shanghai. The Court can find out
from Dah Yuen Li, as to the man named Lau Tsang. The chief
tenant of the house is named Tsang, and I hired my room from
him. I have been detained at the P.S.Bureau for more than three
weeks. I did not tell them that I was a native of Shanse be-
cause I did not want to tell them.
SUMMING UP
Procurator:- According to the evidence we can,
at most, decide that the accused attempted to propagate commun-
ism so the accused should not be found guilty, as attempts to
propagate communism is not punishable according to law.

Subject (in full) S.S.D.C. Search Warrant No.5424.

Made by D.S. Moore. Forwarded by

Ref the attachment of Officer i/c Special Branch
concerning the recent arrest of one Lee Dah Yeu (李大有) alias
Lau Tsang (老張) at 1034 Dah Yeu Lee off Macao Road.
The original information concerning this address was
furnished by a Special Branch informer, who asserted that "Lau
Tsang" was a participant at secret communist meetings held in the
Western District. In the interests of the Special Branch it is
highly undesirable that the informer and the accused be confronted
with each other, therefore the possibility of strengthening the
case against the accused from that angle is somewhat hopeless.
Upon arrival of the Police party at the home of the accused
at 11.15 p.m. October 11, 1932 in execution of S.S.D.C. Search
Warrant No. 5424, all rooms in the house were visited. A small
back room was found to be locked and ostensibly unoccupied, but
on further examination, it was found to contain a loft in which
the accused was sleeping. The accused was awakened and asked
his name and stated that it was Lee Dah Yeu (李大有). It is
peculiar that the alleyway in which his house is located is called
the Dah Yeu Lee and it was thereupon supposed that the name he
gave was the first he could think of on being awakened.
In support of the theory that Lee Dah Yeu and Lau Tseng are
identical, I attach herewith an envelope addressed to Tsang Soong
San (張松山) found in the sleeping place of the accused.
The four communist handbills produced as evidence against
the accused were found by D.S. Moore and Clerk Van Ti-fao concealed
under the straw matting on which the accused was sleeping.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

关于此地址的原始情报由一名特务科线人提供，该线人称“刘藏”参与了在西区举行的秘密共产党会议。出于特务科的利益，极不宜让线人与被告当面对质，因此从那个角度加强针对被告的案件的可能性有些渺茫。
1932年10月11日晚上11点15分，警方在执行上海特区地方法院搜查令编号 5424 时到达被告住所，视察了屋内所有房间。发现一间小的后屋锁着，表面上无人居住，但经进一步检查，发现里面有一个阁楼，被告正睡在其中。被告被唤醒并被询问姓名，他声称名叫李大有（李大有）。奇怪的是，他房子所在的弄堂叫大有里，因此推测这是他醒来时能想到的第一个名字。
为了支持李大有和刘曾（Lau Tseng）是同一人的理论，我随信附上在被告睡觉的地方发现的一个写给张松山（張松山）的信封。
作为针对被告的证据出示的四份共产主义传单，是由 D.S. Moore 和职员 Van Ti-fao 在被告睡觉的草席下发现的。

Raid on Communist Bases - four arrests

Acting on the authority of search warrants, the Municipal
Police, on the night of October 11/12, conducted a series of raids
on communist bases in the Settlement, and effected the arrest of
four persons reported to be responsible for carrying out
communist activities among workers of industrial concerns in
the Western District, and seized a quantity of communist
documents. The particulars of the raids are given hereunder :-

1. 1408 Yuan Yui Lee (源裕里), Hart Road. A quantity of
communist documents was seized in an upstairs back room and
the wanted man Siao Song (小王) alias Ho Sau-ming (胡少敏),
who made an unsuccessful attempt to escape over the roofs of
the adjoining houses, was apprehended on the drying stage of
house No. 1409. This man is reported to be a member of the
Central Committee of the local Communist Party who was
recently sent by the Party to direct communist activities
among workers in the Western District.

2. No. 540 Zoong Oen Lee (崇安里), Haiphong Road. A quantity
of communist literature was found in the room over the kitchen
and two persons, one named Woo Yoong (吴熊), a member of
the Western District Committee of the Communist Party, and one
named Liu Yeong Foong (刘永峰) were arrested.

3. No. 1034 Dah You Li (大有里), Macao Road. A small quantity
of communist literature was seized and a man named Lau Chang
(老修) alias Lee Dah You (李大有), who is reported to be
the director of workers in demonstrations, was arrested.

4. 1570 Ying Hwa Lee (英華里), Hobson Road. A quantity of
communist literature was seized in the kitchen room, but the
wanted man was absent at the time of the raid.

The arrested persons will appear before Court on October 13
when a remand will be asked for in order to enable the Police
to make further enquiries.

1. 哈同路（Hart Road）源裕里1408号。在楼上后屋缴获大量共产党文件，通缉犯小王（Siao Song），化名胡少敏（Ho Sau-ming），在试图翻越邻近房屋屋顶逃跑未遂后，在1409号的晒台上被捕。据报此人是当地共产党中央委员会成员，最近被党派往指导西区工人的共产党活动。

2. 海防路（Haiphong Road）崇安里540号。在厨房上方的房间里发现大量共产主义文献，两人被捕，一人名为吴熊（Woo Yoong），系共产党西区委员会成员，另一人名为刘永峰（Liu Yeong Foong）。

3. 澳门路大有里1034号。缴获少量共产主义文献，逮捕了一名名叫老修（Lau Chang），化名李大有（Lee Dah You）的男子，据报他是示威活动中工人的指挥者。

4. 赫司克路（Hobson Road）英華里1570号。在厨房房间内缴获大量共产主义文献，但突袭时通缉犯不在场。

本人与刑事侦探主任（C.D.C.）170号会同特别科侦探前往搜查令所述地址，发现被告正在一楼的一间小房间内睡觉，其持有两份共产主义宣传册，译文附后。

被告自称名为 Bee Dah You（音译），不承认自己是刘藏（Lau Tsang）。然而，当侦探最初进入时，房主称屋内无人，直至进行搜查后，才在锁着的房门后的房间内发现被告。此外，房间内未发现任何衣物或物品能表明被告并非刘藏。

被告将于明日，即1932年10月12日，出庭受审于副巡官法庭（S.S.D Court）。

workers employed in the Kiwa Cotton Mill bearing on the
amalgamation of factories and the dismissal of workers
in large numbers," purporting to have emanated from the
Propaganda Department of the Shanghai Western Special
District Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, four
copies of which were seized during the course of a raid
at No.1034 Dah Yeu Li (    ), Macao Road at 11.30 p.m.
October 11, 1932.

Labourers.

The capitalists in the Kiwa Cotton Mill have oppressed
and treated us in the worst possible manner. Recently they
have intended to amalgamate Nos.2 and 3 factories into one
factory. Following this, they will certainly dismiss those
workers who receive high pay and who are unfit for their work.
This is urgently desired by the Japanese capitalists in order
that they may close down the factories as a protest against the
victories of the Red Armies of the Chinese labourers and peasants.
We should recall the blood massacre by the capitalists.
They close factories, compel female workers to pick coal and
bring female workers to Chapel to be raped, expel workers
out of quarters by force of arms, and the Japanese imperialists
will occupy Shanghai again.
We should persist in opposing the closure and
amalgamation of factories, establish a "Close Factory Committee"
and "Oppose Amalgamate Factory Committee", declare strikes
and hold flying meetings at the gates of factories as a turn
to the closure and amalgamation of factories by the
capitalists. Join the Communist Party in hundreds and
thousands as a protest against the second occupation of
Shanghai by the Japanese imperialists. Declare strikes
and participate in Mass Meetings in the commemorations of
the "September 18 Anniversary."

工人们。

吉华纱厂的资本家以最恶劣的方式压迫和对待我们。最近，他们打算将第二和第三工厂合并为一个工厂。随后，他们必将解雇那些薪水较高且被认为不胜任工作的工人。这是日本资本家迫切希望的，以便他们通过关闭工厂来抗议中国工农红军的胜利。我们要回想资本家的血腥屠杀。他们关闭工厂，强迫女工拣煤，将女工带到教堂（Chapel）实施强奸，武装驱逐工人离开宿舍，而日本帝国主义者将再次占领上海。
我们要坚持反对关闭和合并工厂，成立“关厂委员会”和“反对合并工厂委员会”，宣布罢工，并在工厂门口举行飞行集会，以应对资本家关闭和合并工厂的行径。成千上万地加入共产党，以抗议日本帝国主义者第二次占领上海。宣布罢工，并参加纪念“九一八周年”的群众大会。
